messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a spike of microbursts this morning that pushed a subset of tenants past our 99th P99 SLO for 3min. Looks like continuous-batcher queues filled and we started dropping to fallback smaller model, but tail latency still bad. attaching grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abcd1234
maya: ugh. which pool/host? any commonalities across tenants?
sam: mostly bursty traffic from mobile product experiments, same cohort on pool-gpu-09. timeline: enqueue growth -> coalesce window expands -> drain slower -> kvcache contention rises -> fallback.
jorge: can you paste the top logs for that host? curious about preempt evictions and whether the admission credits were exhausted.
sam: pasted snippets: ```
[1719009601] ENQUEUE req tenant=tn-42 size=480 tokens
[1719009602] COALESCE join epoch=362 window_ms=17
[1719009603] ADMIT tenant=tn-42 credits=0 -> queued
[1719009610] EVICT tenant=tn-11 reason=starvation
[1719009618] FALLBACK model=smaller-1 triggered
```
li: two quick hypotheses: 1) our coalesce growth is too aggressive during microbursts and stalls admission; 2) kvcache eviction thrash makes generation slower even after batching. either could blow the tail because other tenants get preempted.
nina: agree. also we don't have a fast-path for tiny bursts — we always pay the coalesce latency. maybe run an experiment: if enqueue rate spikes above X for a tenant, route that tenant to a small-window low-latency lane for N seconds.
maya: that sounds promising. but need guardrails: what if lots of tenants flip lanes and we overload the low-latency lane? we need graceful degradation.
jorge: idea: make lane-swap admission conservative using token-affinity signals + probabilistic sampling. i.e., only a fraction of burst requests go to low-latency lane; rest stay in normal coalesce path. that reduces thundering herd.
li: another lever: short-circuit kvcache lookup for tiny responses. add a size-hint on requests and skip heavy cache recovery if expected output < Y tokens. cheaper and faster.
sam: telemetry gaps: we need per-tenant coalesce-window distribution, swap counts, and kvcache eviction rate. current metrics are per-host only. without that we can't test thresholds.
nina: agree. can we add a tracing tag when we trigger lane-swap + reason (rate, latency, manual)? minimal perf cost.
maya: ops-bot reported a deploy around 1719009400 — could be related. ops-bot: deploy redwood-runtime v2.14.3 rolled to pool-gpu-09 at 1719009420. no rollbacks.
jorge: ok, next steps proposal: 1) add per-tenant coalesce histogram + lane-swap counter (telemetry task), 2) prototype low-latency lane with conservative admission (experiment), 3) add a quick kvcache size-hint path (micro-optim), 4) run canary on pool-gpu-09 for 24h.
li: for the prototype, let's keep config knobs per-tenant so product can opt out if needed. also surfaced fallback policy: prefer model-fallback only after lane-swap fails to reduce double-penalty.
sam: can we ship telemetry before experiment? need at least one 1h window of data to pick thresholds.
nina: i'll own the telemetry dashboard and alerts. will add per-tenant charts + derived rate signal. target to have dashboards by EOD tomorrow.
maya: i'll sketch the low-latency lane admission logic and config. will post a short RFC with interfaces and fallbacks.
jorge: i'll take the kvcache hint path — should be a small change to lookup path and bench it locally.
li: I'll coordinate the canary rollout plan and rollback criteria. suggest: if P99 tail > baseline + 20% or model-fallback rate increases > 2x, rollback.
sam: thanks. one more ask: let's record a short test harness that can simulate microbursts across tenants so we can iterate quickly.
nina: good call — adding a simple load shape generator to the infra playbook.
maya: cool. tagging followups: @nina telemetry, @jorge kvcache, @maya admission-proto, @li canary.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-5231 for telemetry + INF-5232 for admission prototype.
sam: thanks team. will check back after dashboards come up. :thumbsup:
